anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

apparatus: Witte p.96–98. Line 29 L. ca. 2 Z. kept as printed dots.
Mostly unrestored or heavily restored Greek; English does not fill gaps.

choices.why: The world's maker; Origen's point is that this making is not God's first work.
The proper use of 'first' requires that nothing precede.

pass_a_gloss: For the world-making has had a beginning, the Craftsman, yet not having been made first by the Craftsman — for the Craftsman made many things before [gap]. But the things that came to be had a beginning, whether first or second in word. For the first is properly said only of nothing preceding; but beginning is signified upon things beginning, even if they become last. And what is first, this is also beginning; but what is beginning is not already also first.
pass_b_english: For the [making of the world] has had a beginning, [the Creator], yet it was not [made first] by the Creator — [for the] Creator [made many things before] [lacuna]. But [the] things that came to be had a beginning, [whether] first [or second] in word. For [the] first is [properly] said [only] when [nothing] precedes; but beginning is signified of [things that] begin, even if they come last. And whatever is first is also a beginning; but what is a beginning is not already also first.
